newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters union says starts strike at UPS.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters union says starts strike at UPS.

text.p: The Teamsters union said its members began a strike at United Parcels Service on Monday, hours after a last-ditch contract negotiating effort failed.
"The strike has begun," Teamsters union spokesman Rand Wilson told Reuters.
Two hours earlier, at 10 p.m. EDT on Sunday (0200 GMT), Teamsters President Ron Carey left talks with United Parcel
"We have exhausted every possible approach to solve the problem," Carey told reporters.
UPS chief negotiator Dave Murray termed the union decision to abandon the talks "irresponsible," while Labour Secretary Alexis Herman called on the two sides to go back to the bargaining table.

UPS, the largest U.S. parcel carrier, handles 12 million packages a day and employs 301,000 people in the United States, 185,000 of whom are represented by the Teamsters, including package handlers and drivers.
